natalie: Quick summary of today's profiling run for the streaming chat canary: p95 token emit latency at microbatch=8 jumped to ~210ms (was ~115ms at mb=2). p99 also tails out (~480ms). Non-streaming completions show expected throughput gains: mb=16 -> ~18% higher tokens/sec, p95 for whole-response latency only nudged up by ~30ms.

liam: Interesting. Do we have KV cache hit-rate stratified by mb and user session length? My suspicion is kv cache eviction pressure + a kernel fallback on long seqs causing extra jitter.

natalie: Yes — attached profiler snippet shows KV hits drop from 98% -> 72% when mb>=8 under chat load. Also saw more frequent kernel fallback to scalar path for rotary fused kernel on seq>1024. Snippet: 
```
PROF: mb=8 | kv_hit_rate=0.72 | kernel=fused_rotary_v2 -> fallback_count=43 | avg_emit_ms=210
PROF: mb=2 | kv_hit_rate=0.98 | kernel=fused_rotary_v2 -> fallback_count=3 | avg_emit_ms=115
```

anne_dev: TL;DR: for streaming chat users care about per-token emit latency. Larger mb batches amortize GPU work but increase queuing and KV conflict, which hurts tails. Proposal: dynamic heuristic where streaming=true caps mb at 4 for short seq sessions, and non-streaming completions can scale to 8/16. Pseudo-config: 
```json
{"batching": {"streaming_max_mb": 4, "completion_max_mb": 16, "kv_warm_threshold": 0.85}}
```

prakash: Related regression note — last week's kernel change (fused_rotary_v2) improved median throughput but introduced expensive path for cold cache sequences. I can reproduce locally: cold KV + mb>=8 spikes CPU scheduling while kernel tries to allocate temp tensors. We should consider a quick rollback or a targeted revert for long-seq path.

perf-bot: perf-alert: 2026-03-16T18:02Z | job=canary-streaming | metric=p95_emit_latency | baseline=120ms | now=210ms | delta=+75% :warning:

liam: Two practical levers: 1) prefer lower mb for streaming requests (mb=2-4) to reduce queueing and improve KV locality; 2) for non-streaming route accept mb=8-16 and enable prefix/KV prefetch when session is warm. Also instrument kernel-selection logs with request id so we can correlate fallback_count -> tail samples.

santiago: Another angle: tune microbatch release policy so partial batches flush earlier when oldest-wait > X ms. For streaming, X should be low (5-10ms). This way we don't wait for full mb to maximize throughput at cost of latency. Example: 
```
batch_release: {max_wait_ms: 8, min_batch_size: 1}
```

anne_dev: We should add an A/B with three arms: (A) static mb cap 4 for streaming, (B) dynamic release flush with max_wait_ms=8, (C) baseline. Measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput over 24h. Include kernel-fallback sampling and kv_hit_rate tagging.

natalie: Agreed. Action items: @prakash create revert-runbook for fused_rotary_v2 long-seq path (hotfix plan), @liam add kernel-selection + request-id tagging (logs + structured metric). @anne_dev add batching config and rollout plan (A/B). @santiago add release-policy change and sampling. I'll kick off the A/B tomorrow morning and post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
